subject: Acme: Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Simmons <jenna@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Acme: Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Jenna — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard and the cost/TCO levers we discussed so your team can validate assumptions.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Large steady-state token volume from chat+system prompts (roughly 100-200M tokens / month).
- Budget constraint: priority to keep inference spend under ~$10k/mo.
- High variability in peak latency under current multitenant setup; affects UX for real-time features.
- Need for predictable billing and a path to pilot without long procurement.

TCO & levers we discussed (ballpark estimates):
- Baseline (their current): ~160M tokens/mo -> estimated ~$18k/mo (their current hosted provider + some under-utilized batching).
- Redwood optimized run (batching + prefix/KV caching + quantized model): potential ~55-70% reduction -> target ~$6-8k/mo.
- Dedicated footprint (reserved capacity) for predictable latency: increases fixed cost but reduces variable token cost +/- improves SLA.

Assumptions on the ballpark model above: token mix = 70% generation, 30% embeddings/short prompts; average response length 120 tokens; effective batching improvements depend on median concurrency (we assumed 8-12 RPS).

Next steps (agreed on call):
1) I’ll share the TCO workbook (attached) with the assumptions & sensitivity knobs.
2) If you can send 2-3 days of request logs (anonymized) we’ll run a sample run to get a more accurate estimate and recommended config (batch size, cache TTLs, quantization profile).
3) Schedule a 60-minute deep-dive next week to walk the model-level breakdown and a live demo of batching/KV cache impact.

Attachments: acme_tco_model.xlsx (TCO workbook), redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (pricing + capacity options).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times.

— Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks Jenna — answers below and a short sensitivity callout so you can see which knobs matter most.

Pilot scope (90 days): yes — we can design a constrained pilot to stay within $10k with these guardrails:
- Cap on peak throughput and soft throttling after X RPS to protect budget (we’ll set an alert).
- Use a quantized 4-bit model variant for batch-heavy flows and a slightly higher-precision variant for low-latency user-facing calls.

Key assumptions behind the 55-70% savings:
- Batching: median effective batch size = 6-10 tokens/req (depends on concurrency). For chat-style flows where multiple users concurrently generate short responses, batching reduces per-token overhead by ~30-40%.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repetitive system prompts and reused context, we assume a 20-40% cache hit rate on the KV cache based on the sample workloads we’ve seen. Cache hits skip full attention compute and save ~20-35% of cost on those requests.
- Quantization: using INT4/FP16 hybrid profiles reduces model memory footprint and per-token compute by 15-25% with minimal quality degradation for your use cases (we’ll include evals).

Estimated p95 latency impact (examples):
- Optimized hosted (batching + cache): p95 ~450-700 ms for median prompt sizes in our pilot assumptions.
- Dedicated reserved pool: p95 ~200-400 ms (more predictable, higher fixed cost). Exact numbers depend on model selection & avg response length — we’ll run the sample logs to produce an expected latency curve.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Run the TCO workbook sensitivity matrix and highlight the configuration that fits within $10k for 90 days.
- Send a short template for the sanitized logs (column names + anonymization steps).
- Propose two 60-min slots (Wed 3/31 1pm PST or Thu 4/1 2pm PST) for the deep-dive — either works for us.

Marissa — can you own the sample-run and TCO sensitivity and share preliminary numbers by EOD Friday?

— Rishi
